newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- deals price after data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- deals price after data.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were slightly softer after release of inflation data Wednesday, as pricings on the week's largest new issues got underway.

The Labor Department reported that the Consumer Price Index for January rose just 0.1 percent, less than the 0.3 percent increase economists had expected and further support for the view that the Federal Reserve will hold interest rates steady for now.
Fixed income markets initially rose after the data, but then turned lower when support evaporated.
"There's not much of a follow-through on it," one muni trader said. "It's coming off a bit now."

A second trader said, however, that any negative sentiment is being tempered by the lack of supply. The problem, he said, is that the supply that is finally appearing on the horizon will be priced at the high end of the current range, which he identified as a 6.50 percent on the government long bond.
The 30-year bond was off 8/32 at 100-24/32 to yield 6.57 percent.
In the new issue market, Smith Barney Inc said it tentatively priced Hempstead Industrial Development Agency, N.Y.'s $249 million bond deal at a top yield of 5.15 percent in 2009.
Other action Wednesday includes a $189.8 million Florida Board of Education competitive deal at 1100 EST and a $271 million California Public Works negotiated offering, through Bear Stearns & Co.
Wednesday's municipal bond sales are expected to total $1.3 billion in 33 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

In debt futures, the March municipal contract was 7/32 lower at 117-23/32. The March T-bond contract lost 8/32 at 113-19/32. The MOB spread was 132 ticks, widening one tick from 131 at the close on Tuesday.

Among actively traded secondary bonds, bids on Dade County, Fla., FGIC water and sewer 5-1/4s of 2026 were unchanged at 5.51 percent net. Texas Turnpike Authority FGIC 5-1/4s of 2023 were also unchanged at 5.51 percent net.
